content: When a customer demands a specific test, perform it immediately without unnecessary confirmations. Use the 'test-first, confirm-later' approach.
Avoid placeholder text or scripted phrases that don't make sense. Always prepare real data or be ready to improvise with accurate information.
For skeptical customers, use the 'prove it' technique: let the customer see the product perform under their exact conditions.
If the customer is impatient, minimize confirmations and focus on action. One confirmation is enough; multiple confirmations risk losing the customer.
In a remote demo, ensure all technical terms and numbers are accurate and relevant to the customer's context.

name: Test-First Confirmation
condition: When a customer asks for a specific performance test, especially if they are impatient or skeptical.
example: Customer: 'Does it lag with 20 layers?' Salesperson: 'Let me show you right now. I'll open 20 layers and switch between them. Watch the screen.'

name: Technical Anchor
condition: When a customer compares with a competitor (e.g., Procreate) and highlights a weakness.
example: Customer: 'Procreate pixelates at high zoom.' Salesperson: 'That's because Procreate uses raster sampling. Our device uses vector-linked texture maps, so the grain stays sharp at any zoom. Let me demonstrate.'

name: Impatience Deflection
condition: When a customer shows impatience with confirmations or questions.
example: Customer: 'Stop confirming and just do it.' Salesperson: 'You're right. Let me switch layers now. Watch the screen.'

objection: Procreate sometimes pixelates at high zoom.
rebuttal_template: I understand your concern. Let me show you right now on this device: I'll open a 20-layer canvas, zoom in to 800%, and paint a stroke. Watch the grain—it stays sharp because GoPaint uses vector-linked texture maps, not raster sampling. You can see for yourself.

objection: I need to see rapid layer switching at high zoom.
rebuttal_template: Absolutely. Watch as I switch layers 1, 5, 10, 15, 20 at this zoom level. No lag, no pixelation. This is the vector engine in action.
What specific test would convince you? Let's do it right now. I want you to leave here confident in the performance.
